ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 07/2022/QH15 dated 15 November 2022 (effective 1 March 2023); Decree No. 19/2023/ND-CP dated 5 May 2023 detailing the AML Law; Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 dated 17 June 2020; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP dated 4 January 2021 on enterprise registration; Investment Law No. 61/2020/QH14 dated 17 June 2020; and State Bank of Viet Nam guidance on customer due diligence and beneficial ownership reporting.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Registration Certificate of the Foreign Ultimate Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registrar of companies in the ultimate parent's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Vietnamese Consular Legalization at the Embassy/Consulate of Viet Nam in the issuing country; if the issuing country is an Apostille Contracting Party and Viet Nam's accession to the Hague Apostille Convention becomes effective at filing date, an apostille may be accepted in lieu — verify current MOFA notice.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent charter/operating license of the Foreign Ultimate Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent commercial court/tax authority of the foreign parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Vietnamese Consular Legalization (or acceptable apostille if the issuing state is an Apostille Contracting Party and accepted by Viet Nam at filing date).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the local incorporator and establishing the Offshore Development Center
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors / Shareholders' Meeting of the foreign parent company, notarized in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the origin jurisdiction, Vietnamese Consular Legalization, and certified Vietnamese translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport / legal identity document of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner, legal representative, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/immigration authority of each individual's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with certificate conformity, Vietnamese Consular Legalization (or accepted apostille), and sworn Vietnamese translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds evidence for the foreign parent / ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank or licensed auditor where the foreign parent or UBO maintains accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, Vietnamese Consular Legalization (or accepted apostille), and certified Vietnamese translation.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening standards: Conduct risk-based enhanced due diligence on all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and authorized representatives prior to name reservation. Screening must cover the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK OFSI consolidated list, and the State Bank of Viet Nam warning/blacklist. PEP identification must cover immediate family members and close associates using at least two independent databases. Negative news/adverse media and source-of-wealth verification are required. Re-run screening every 30 days from the start of pre-incorporation due diligence until IRC/ERC issuance, then annually or on any trigger event. All results, search logs, and decisions must be preserved in the AML/CFT file under Articles 13-17 of Decree No. 19/2023/ND-CP.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) at https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn and online public services at https://dichvucong.gov.vn
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: An enterprise name must be in Vietnamese, using the Vietnamese alphabet, with accented Vietnamese letters as applicable; it may include Arabic numerals, symbols, and the statutory entity-form prefix 'Công ty TNHH' for a limited liability company. The full Vietnamese name should be followed by the registered name to ensure uniqueness. A transliterated foreign name or abbreviation may appear in brackets but must not be identical or confusingly similar to a previously registered enterprise and must not violate national traditions, culture, or social order.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: "Đảng" (Communist Party) or other political party names
"Quốc hội" (National Assembly), "Chính phủ" (Government), and other sovereign organ names without consent
"Bộ", "Tổng cục", "Uỷ ban", "Viện" and other state-agency organ names unless the competent agency consents in writing
"Công an", "Quân đội", "Viện kiểm sát", "Tòa án" and armed-forces or judicial authority terms
"Ngân hàng" (bank), "Chứng khoán" (securities), "Bảo hiểm" (insurance), "Kiểm toán" (audit), "Quỹ tín dụng" (credit fund) unless the enterprise holds the required sector-specific license
Words contrary to national historical and cultural traditions, social ethics, or public order
A name identical or confusingly similar to a name already registered by another enterprise operating in Viet Nam
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of receiving written rejection from the Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI), file an administrative complaint directly to the Director of the DPI under Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13. In parallel, correct the proposed name and resubmit through the National Enterprise Registration Portal, which is usually the fastest remedy. If the DPI upholds the rejection or fails to decide within 30 days, initiate an administrative lawsuit before the competent provincial People's Court under Law on Administrative Procedures No. 93/2015/QH13. Engage Vietnamese counsel to verify whether the rejection is based on Article 38 of Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, and request interim relief only if delay would cause irreparable harm.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or mailbox address is not permissible as the sole registered office. Article 42 of Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 requires the enterprise to maintain its head office at a lawful physical address in Viet Nam. A serviced office with an executed physical lease, signage, and personnel may be accepted as an interim registered office; however, an Offshore Development Center must maintain substantive operational facilities, records, and personnel at that address to withstand tax, labor, and immigration inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high for a foreign-invested IT ODC: estimated 30% likelihood of unannounced inspection during the first 12 months and up to 65% within 36 months, particularly if the entity claims tax incentives, makes cross-border payments, or applies foreign contractor taxation. Unannounced physical on-site inspections by tax authorities, labor inspectors, and fire-safety agencies are permitted during normal business hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14, particularly Articles 25, 74-79, 153, 196-202; Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 38-39 and 41; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration, as amended by Decree No. 47/2021/ND-CP and Decree No. 122/2021/ND-CP.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office and Investment Registration Division under the Agency for Business Registration, Department of Planning and Investment of the relevant province or centrally run city (Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi), operating via the National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration (Giấy đề nghị đăng ký doanh nghiệp) submitted through the National Business Registration Portal, together with the Company Charter, list of members, Capital Contribution Commitment, and Investment Registration Certificate (for foreign-invested projects).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for software/IT services LLCs; charter capital is freely determined by members but must be adequate for the business scale. Foreign investors must contribute the full charter capital within 90 days of the Enterprise Registration Certificate, through a capital contribution bank account (no escrow is statutorily required). Where a conditional business line is triggered, relevant legal capital may apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE MEMBERS/OWNER OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY — RESOLUTION NO. 01/2025. Passed in writing on [date] by the sole member/all members pursuant to the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and the Company Charter. RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The charter capital is VND [amount], divided into [number] capital contribution portions allocated to members as set out in the list of members attached hereto. Each member irrevocably subscribes to such portions and undertakes to contribute them in full within 90 days of the Enterprise Registration Certificate into the company's capital contribution account at [licensed bank and branch]. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the company is [full address in Vietnam]. The General Director/Chairperson is authorized to complete all notifications, filings, and signages for the registered office. 3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: The members appoint [Name] as Chairperson of the Members Council, [Name] as General Director/Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Accountant, and, if applicable, [Name] as the company's authorized representative under Article 12 of the Law on Enterprises, each with powers as described in the Company Charter, including opening bank accounts, executing contracts, and filing legal documents. 4. AUTHORIZATION FOR INCORPORATION AGENT: The Chairperson and General Director are jointly authorized to engage counsel, submit all applications, certify documents, pay fees, register tax, obtain corporate seals, and take all necessary acts for incorporation and initial licensing. This Resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Investment Registration Certificate (for foreign-invested ODC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Registration Division, Department of Planning and Investment of the province/city of the registered office (via the National Investment Registration System).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Investment Registration Application (Giấy đề nghị thực hiện dự án đầu tư) with a project proposal describing the offshore software development center (ODC), estimated charter capital, funding schedule, proposed registered office, and EPE status if applicable. Attach legalized corporate documents of the foreign investor, passport copies for individual investors, financial evidence of investment capital, and lease letter of intent. The Department of Planning and Investment must issue the Investment Registration Certificate within 15 working days for projects not subject to approval. Online submission using the National Investment Registration System is recommended. Retain a complete docket at the project site. If the authority issues a query, amend the dossier as requested and resubmit promptly.
required_dossiers: Investment Registration Application
Project proposal / business plan for ODC
Legalized and notarized Vietnamese translation of the foreign investor's incorporation documents (or passport of an individual investor)
Financial statement or bank confirmation of the investor's ability to contribute capital
Power of attorney to the authorized representative/law firm
Lease agreement or letter of intent for the office premises
Documents confirming proposed export processing enterprise (EPE) status, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is incomplete, supplement within the timeframe stated by the authority; if the Investment Registration Certificate is refused, file a written complaint with the Chairman of the Provincial People's Committee or exercise administrative court remedies under the Law on Administrative Procedures (Law No. 24/2015/QH13).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, notarize, and approve the Company Charter and internal governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Phòng Công chứng / Văn phòng Công chứng) for notarization of the Charter, members' capital contribution list and owner's resolution; the investors' decision approving the Charter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Charter in Vietnamese in accordance with Article 24 of the Law on Enterprises, covering company name, registered office, business scope, charter capital, members, governance, duties of officers, capital contribution timelines, and liquidation. The sole member (for single-member LLC) must issue a written Owner's Decision adopting the Charter and capital contribution schedule; for multi-member LLC, all members sign the Charter and capital contribution list at a members' meeting. Notarize the Charter and the list of members by a Vietnamese notary public, and ensure all foreign documents are legalized and translated per Vietnamese law. Prepare a notarized appointment of legal representative and a power of attorney for the incorporation agent.
required_dossiers: Company Charter (Điều lệ công ty) in Vietnamese
Owner's Decision / Members' Meeting Minutes adopting the Charter
List of members (Danh sách thành viên) with signature and capital contribution portions
Notarized identity documents of members and legal representative
Legalized and notarized Vietnamese translation of corporate documents of any corporate member
Power of attorney appointing an authorized representative or law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is refused, correct deficiencies, re-submit to the same notary or another notary; complaints against a notary's refusal may be lodged with the Department of Justice (Sở Tư pháp) under the Notary Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Application for Enterprise Registration and obtain the Enterprise Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Department of Planning and Investment, via the National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic Application for Enterprise Registration (Giấy đề nghị đăng ký doanh nghiệp), upload the notarized Charter, list of members, legalized identity documents, and the Investment Registration Certificate; verify that the company name is unique and not confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise. The authority must issue the Enterprise Registration Certificate within 3 working days from a valid submission. Once issued, download the electronic certificate, verify the accuracy of all fields, and proceed to seal creation, tax registration, and bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Application for Enterprise Registration
Company Charter (notarized)
List of members or sole member's declaration
Notarized copies of passport/ID of legal representative
Legalized copies of documents for corporate members
Investment Registration Certificate (if foreign-invested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, read the authority's written refusal, correct the errors, and resubmit; appeal to the Department of Planning and Investment or initiate administrative court proceedings. If the name conflicts, select a new name and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Seal creation, post-registration publication, tax registration, and bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seal engraving vendor (private entity); Police Department for seal registration; National Business Registration Portal for publication; General Department of Taxation via local sub-department; licensed commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Enterprise Registration Certificate, have the corporate seal created at a licensed engraving shop and register the seal specimen with the provincial Police Department through the national portal within the required period (no separate approval required; notification is sufficient under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP). Publish corporate information (company name, head office, capital, legal representative) on the National Business Registration Portal within 30 days of certificate issuance. Confirm automatic tax registration and obtain the statement of tax identification number from the tax authority. Open a corporate bank account (capital contribution account and operational account) with a licensed bank; deposit the charter capital within the statutory 90-day schedule or as stated in the Investment Registration Certificate. Complete statistics registration and, if imports/exports exist, register as an exporter/importer via the customs authority.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Seal specimen and seal registration declaration
Charter and legal representative ID for bank forms
Investment Registration Certificate
Tax registration declaration (NT-99 or automatic code confirmation)
Beneficial owner/ultimate beneficial owner declarations for bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If seal registration is rejected, correct the specimen format and re-file with the police portal; if tax registration is not automatic, file directly at the Department of Taxation. If the bank delays account opening, provide certified English/Vietnamese translations and complete additional KYC/AML documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lease/confirm physical premises, fire safety inspection, and occupational health clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fire Prevention and Rescue Police under the Provincial Police Department; Department of Science and Technology/Division of Occupational Health (MOH) for workplace environment monitoring; local construction authority for structural acceptance (if new construction or fit-out requires permit).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a valid office lease agreement and verify the building has a Fire Safety Design Approval and Fire Safety Acceptance Certificate. For fit-out works requiring construction permits, obtain the building permit and then a fire safety acceptance certificate from the local Fire Police for the ODC floor/office. Carry out workplace environment monitoring (illumination, noise, air quality, thermal environment) through a licensed agency per QCVN 22:2016/BYT and QCVN 26:2016/BYT; prepare an occupational safety and health plan, emergency procedures, and training records. If the building is within an EPE/industrial zone, coordinate with the Zone Management Board for the facility acceptance and obtain confirmations of wastewater/sewer connection and waste collection service.
required_dossiers: Office lease agreement and a copy of the building's certified fire safety title/certificate
Fire safety acceptance certificate for the leased area (or evidence of the lessor's valid building certificate)
Construction permit and completion acceptance (if the ODC performs fit-out works requiring permits)
Occupational environment monitoring test report
Workplace safety and emergency plans
Zone management board acceptance (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fire safety certification is outstanding due to the lessor's deficient building compliance, require the lessor to remediate or relocate; the ODC may alternatively retrofit the leased floor and obtain a separate acceptance. For occupational monitoring, engage another licensed agency. Any administrative refusal can be appealed to the director of the relevant Police Department or the Provincial People's Committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Information and Communications (MIC) for ICT software enterprises; Department of Planning and Investment / Export Processing and Industrial Zone Authority for EPE/industrial zone licensing; Fire Prevention and Rescue Police for physical fire safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Enterprise Registration Certificate (with the line 'Software development services' and related IT activities) — no separate industrial operating license is required for a general software development/ODC under ISIC 6202. If the ODC operates in an export processing zone, the Investment Registration Certificate will note EPE status (export processing enterprise). For certain IT services involving provision to other enterprises in an EPE, an 'ET1/ET2' registration may be recorded in the investment dossier.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) / provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE), with support from EPE industrial zone management boards where applicable; environmental protection regulations under Law No. 72/2020/QH14 and Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV — not subject to a full EIA report; the software office/ODC is a light non-industrial service facility requiring only environmental registration (đăng ký môi trường) with the competent authority (provincial or EPE management board) and waste management compliance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For domestic wastewater from office facilities, comply with QCVN 14:2008/BTNMT (effluent standards for domestic wastewater) or the local sewerage acceptance criteria; monitor drinking water and sanitary water quality; for office generators/backup diesel generators (if any) comply with QCVN 19:2009/BTNMT for flue gas emissions; hazardous waste (e-waste, batteries, fluorescent tubes, inks) must be classified, declared, and transferred to licensed waste treatment contractors per Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP; greenhouse gas inventory obligations may apply at a later compliance date if operating in an EPE with large energy consumption, but generally not for a standard ODC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises must have a valid Fire Safety Acceptance Certificate issued by the provincial Fire Police (for buildings meeting the regulatory thresholds), a fire safety compliance declaration, and a licensed evacuation/emergency plan. Occupational safety and health clearances: workplace environment monitoring must meet QCVN 22:2016/BYT (lighting), QCVN 26:2016/BYT (microclimate), and QCVN 24:2016/BYT (noise), with reports retained in the company's health and safety dossier; water quality monitoring for sanitary facilities; structural load clearance is the lessor's responsibility but the ODC must, before fit-out, verify loading capacity and obtain construction/fit-out completion acceptance as required. Employee health examinations and training records under the Occupational Safety and Health Law No. 84/2015/QH13 must be maintained together with a workplace exposure register.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế, GDT), Ministry of Finance of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam; national e-tax portal: https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn; e-invoice portal: https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn; one-stop business registration gateway: https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; governing instruments: Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14, Decree 126/2020/ND-CP, Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A 100% foreign-invested LLC automatically obtains its 13-digit Tax Identification Number (Mã số thuế, MST) through the integrated one-stop registration procedure: the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) issues the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) and transfers the enterprise record electronically to the local tax office, which issues the MST without a separate tax application; the LLC then activates its e-tax account using a digital certificate/PKI token and files its VAT and CIT registrations from the first taxable period. Foreign contractors without a Vietnamese establishment that earn Vietnam-source income must instead register under the Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) regime and obtain a separate MST from the GDT; offshore software suppliers without local establishment must register, declare, and pay through the GDT foreign-supplier e-portal. No minimum paid-in capital or equity threshold is a precondition for tax ID issuance, and the LLC's foreign-invested ownership does not alter its taxpayer registration pathway.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vietnam does not statutorily provide check-the-box entity elections or hybrid-mismatch elections comparable to other jurisdictions; available statutory elections and operational regimes include: (i) under the FCT regime, an offshore contractor may elect the deduction method (tax on assessed net income) instead of the direct gross-take method where full Vietnamese accounting and transfer-pricing documentation is maintained; (ii) the LLC may apply the VAT credit-invoice method rather than the direct deduction method where statutory eligibility exists; (iii) the LLC may register for and apply CIT incentive statuses (e.g., software enterprise, high-technology park, EPZ/export-processing enterprise) by reflecting qualifying investment in its tax determination files; (iv) an offshore supplier without local establishment may elect the simplified GDT e-portal filing regime for VAT plus FCT; no entity reclassification or hybrid-mismatch election exists in Vietnamese law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV; Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam) is the sole monetary, banking and foreign-exchange control authority, administering the exchange-control framework pursuant to the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam, the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange No. 05/2005/PL-UBTVQH11 as amended by Ordinance No. 07/2013/UBTVQH13, and Circular No. 15/2015/TT-NHNN on foreign-exchange management for foreign direct investment. The Ministry of Finance and its General Department of Taxation operate the complementary tax-clearance gate on profit, dividend and other current-account remittance outflows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Viet Nam has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations and maintains current-account convertibility, so the ODC may make and receive payments for software services, royalties, intercompany charges and lawfully declared dividends without prior SBV approval on the underlying current transaction, subject to documentary verification by the servicing bank. The VND is nevertheless a managed, non-freely-convertible currency on the capital account: all charter-capital equity, shareholder loan injections, capital repatriation, loan repayments and liquidation proceeds must enter or leave Viet Nam exclusively through the mandatory Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) maintained at an SBV-licensed credit institution. Profit remittance hurdles in practice are: completion of annual statutory audit by an approved auditing firm; final corporate income tax settlement with no outstanding tax, social insurance or customs liabilities; evidence of distributable profits per audited financial statements; a board resolution declaring the dividend; and a DICA balance sufficient to settle the remitted foreign currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the post-2015 regime there is no mandatory minimum surrender or conversion ratio for export proceeds of a foreign-invested enterprise; the former 30% forced-conversion requirement was abrogated by Circular No. 15/2015/TT-NHNN. The binding statutory disciplines for the ISIC 6202 offshore development center are: (i) full repatriation: all foreign-currency receipts from current transactions, including software-services invoices to non-resident clients, must be transferred into the ODC's Foreign Currency Account (FCA) at an authorised credit institution within 15 days of receipt; (ii) timing: export-of-services proceeds must be collected within the contractual payment period, with a prudential banking baseline of 90 days from completion of the exported service where documentary collection or open-account settlement is used, and longer contractual tenors accepted on proof of the underlying agreement; (iii) conversion: the enterprise retains freedom to hold USD in the FCA or sell it to the authorised bank, but any conversion must be executed through the licensed bank at the prevailing rate and unlicensed retail conversion or off-shore netting arrangements are unlawful.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam (Vietcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: DICA - Direct Investment Capital Account for charter capital, shareholder loans and capital/profit repatriation; FCA/VND Operating Account for current transactions, payroll, vendors and tax payments

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam (BIDV)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: DICA plus FCA/VND Operating Account; flagship state-influenced bank for licensed FDI enterprises with strong SBV relationship

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Industry and Trade (VietinBank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: DICA plus FCA/VND Operating Account; robust corporate treasury, SWIFT MT103 and documentary LC processing

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Technological and Commercial Joint Stock Bank (Techcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: DICA plus FCA/VND Operating Account; advanced digital onboarding and automated e-banking treasury desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (MB Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: DICA plus FCA/VND Operating Account; competent AML/KYC units with technology-sector experience
DICA plus FCA/VND Operating Account; SME-oriented digital treasury and liquidity products

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW as a primary or statutory banking rail; CONDITIONAL as an ancillary collection concentrator only. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business/B2B, Payoneer, Airwallex and similar) do not hold a Vietnamese banking licence or foreign-bank branch licence under the Law on Credit Institutions and cannot lawfully open the mandatory DICA, maintain a Vietnamese-locale IBAN, settle VND, or perform treasury clearing inside Viet Nam. The permissible architecture for this ODC is: non-Vietnamese clients may remit USD/EUR into the offshore EMI wallet as a collection convenience, the EMI sweeps the consolidated balance to the onshore licensed FCA via SWIFT MT103 within the statutory repatriation discipline, and all invoicing, revenue recognition, tax filings and statutory books remain in the Vietnamese LLC. The EMI must never be used to invoice Vietnamese-resident clients or to pay local payroll in VND, as that would constitute authorised-payment-services and foreign-exchange evasion; the servicing bank must be disclosed of the EMI relationship during onboarding to avoid an undisclosed-channel AML negative.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate: fully remote onboarding of a 100-per-cent foreign-owned LLC is not available under prevailing SBV compliance practice. The Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 14/2022/QH15, effective 1 March 2023, and the SBV customer-due-diligence framework require positive identification of the legal entity, its authorised signatories, its ultimate beneficial owners and controlling persons, and evidence of economic substance. In practice, the foreign legal representative or an authorised Vietnamese-resident officer acting under a notarised and legalised power of attorney must appear physically at the bank branch for biometric identity verification, specimen signature registration, passport verification and activation of the DICA/FCA mandates. Banks generally permit remote pre-screening through scanned constitutive documents and a video interview, but original or bank-certified copies of the Enterprise Registration Certificate, the Investment Registration Certificate, the charter, board resolutions, passports, UBO declarations and the company seal must be physically lodged and verified before the account becomes operational; any zero-physical-presence exception is escalated to the bank's head-office AML committee as a high-risk account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-services exporter (ISIC 6202/NAICS 541512) with a single foreign parent as primary counterparty and low local fixed assets, raising shell-company or transfer-mispricing red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enterprise Registration Certificate and Investment Registration Certificate; complete UBO/shareholder constitution chain; audited or seed-stage financial statements with a board-approved budget; signed offshore development services agreement, SOW and delivery acceptance evidence; arm's-length pricing analysis; contemporaneous Transfer Pricing documentation including Local File and Form No. 03-7/TNDN report; payroll and Social Insurance (BHXH) contribution records; physical office lease and utility evidence in Viet Nam.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO, PEP or sanctioned-jurisdiction exposure in the foreign ownership chain, especially through non-transparent intermediate holding vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and consularly legalised constitutional documents of every intermediate holding entity; UBO declaration annexed to the bank's CDD form; corporate registry extracts from reputable jurisdictions; passport copies of natural-person controllers; OFAC/UN/EU sanctions self-certification and beneficial-owner screening permissibility; source-of-wealth statement evidencing lawful origin of charter capital (parent bank statements, audited retained earnings or sale-and-purchase agreements).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity foreign-currency inflows followed by rapid outbound sweeps, dividend or royalty remittances, creating a pass-through or trade-based money-laundering pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual treasury and cash-flow forecast with projected recurrent flows; underlying client invoices and faithful MT103 correspondence trail; tax clearance on remittance (CIT finalisation, witholding tax payment receipts); intercompany service documentation demonstrating direct benefit and re-charge basis; FCA balance explanations and a signed undertaking to notify the AML officer of material variance; periodic financial statements confirming operating substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on offshore digital EMI wallets or undisclosed digital payment channels, suggesting unlicensed money transmission or concealed FX conversion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensing and regulatory status evidence of the EMI (e.g., FCA, FinCEN, MAS or similar authorisation); read-only access or periodic statements of the EMI wallet shared with the bank; a documented period-end sweep mechanism into the onshore FCA; a board-adopted treasury policy forbidding client payments through unlicensed intermediaries; reconciliation of EMI receipts to invoiced software services and tax declarations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must be routed through the DICA. The foreign parent shall remit charter capital by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the LLC's DICA opened with the mandated relationship bank, with field 70 clearly stating: 'Contribution of charter capital by [Investor Name] under Investment Registration Certificate No. XXX' or 'Shareholder loan drawdown under Facility Agreement dated XXX and SBV foreign-borrowing registration No. XXX'. The bank will verify the remitter's identity, the amount against the IRC/approved capital schedule, and the loan registration or notification requirement under the SBV foreign-borrowing regulations; under the Law on Enterprises, charter capital must be fully contributed within 90 days from the Enterprise Registration Certificate date if no longer schedule is approved. Upon verification, the funds are credited to the DICA and may be converted to VND for opex only against the LLC's written conversion instruction supported by underlying payment obligations. Capital receipts may never pass through third-party or EMI accounts, because the DICA is the exclusive statutory inbound rail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing rails comprise: (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for current-account disbursements, including fees to offshore subcontractors, software royalties, intercompany management charges, loan interest and principal, and profit/dividend remittances, each payment requiring an underlying contract, invoice, tax-withholding evidence (foreign-contractor tax certificates, WHT payment vouchers or FTCKR/CIT clearance) and a lawful purpose code on the bank remittance form; (ii) Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700 issuance and subsequent negotiation/payment) where the ODC procures hardware, software licenses or delivers turn-key IT projects requiring documentary control against shipping documents, proforma invoices and acceptance certificates; (iii) in-country operating expenses must be settled in VND after authorised-bank conversion, because inter-resident foreign-currency settlement outside licensed banks is prohibited; (iv) dividend and statutory capital-reduction remittances require DICA routing plus tax clearance and audited distributable-profit confirmation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright USD/VND FX forwards offered by SBV-licensed credit institutions, with tenor generally capped at 365 days and supported by underlying current-account exposure evidenced by signed software service contracts or invoices.

USD/VND FX swaps (spot-plus-forward or forward flips) executed with licensed domestic banks to align VND operating liquidity with USD export revenue and to square DICA balances during capital repatriation.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (USD/VND CCIRS combined with interest-rate hedging) entered into by the LLC with a licensed bank in connection with a registered foreign-currency shareholder facility, documented under an ISDA/IAF 2002 suite with Vietnamese-law ancillary standby provisions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD/VND are generally not permissible for onshore resident corporates, as the SBV restricts derivative dealing to authorised credit institutions and requires deliverable underlying exposure; the offshore NDF market serves only non-resident counterparties, and the ODC treasury policy should expressly exclude NDF usage to eliminate enforcement risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Report (Bao cao doanh nghiep) filed through the National Business Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment of the licensing province; central National Business Registration Portal managed by the Ministry of Planning and Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year end; calendar-year enterprises must file by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of VND 10-20 million (approx. USD 400-800) under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP; failure to file for 12 consecutive months permits administrative strike-off by removal of the enterprise from the National Business Registration Database and deemed dissolution under the Law on Enterprises 2020

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business license fee payment (le phi mon bai) and fee declaration for the charter capital bracket
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation through the provincial Tax Department via the national e-tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 30 January for existing enterprises; newly incorporated enterprises are exempt for their first calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at 0.03% per day on the unpaid fee, administrative penalties under the Tax Administration Law 2021, and forced collection measures including bank levy and suspension of tax invoices if non-payment persists

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Submission of annual audited financial statements and summarized financial information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment alongside the provincial Tax Department; filing executed via the National Business Registration Portal and e-tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year end; calendar-year enterprises must submit by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to provide financial statements to the licensing authority triggers fines up to VND 15 million under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP and may escalate to coercive measures; the mandatory audit requirement remains enforceable for all foreign-invested enterprises

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax finalization return, annual personal income tax finalization return for employees, and settlement of any tax liabilities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation through the provincial Tax Department using the national electronic tax filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Both the CIT finalization return and the PIT finalization return for the prior calendar year must be submitted and settled no later than 30 March (31 March where the deadline falls on a non-business day)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at 0.03% per day; late filing penalties ranging from 10% to 20% of the assessed under-declared tax; deliberate misdeclaration penalties up to three times the evaded tax under the Law on Tax Administration 2019

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All foreign-invested enterprises, including 100% foreign-owned limited liability companies, are required to have their annual financial statements audited by an independent certified audit firm under the Law on Enterprises 2020 and Decree 17/2012/ND-CP; the obligation applies to every FDI LLC irrespective of revenue or asset size, unless the enterprise is exempted by an express and continuing derogation
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory financial statements are prepared under Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) in accordance with the Law on Accounting 2015, Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC for large enterprises or Circular 133/2016/TT-BTC for small and medium enterprises; IFRS adoption is permitted only for parent-level consolidated reporting by qualifying enterprises under the selective accelerator regime

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Viet Nam does not maintain a standalone annual UBO return; however, the Anti-Money Laundering Law 2022 (Law 05/2022/QH15) and Decree 06/2023/ND-CP require continuous customer due diligence and preservation of updated beneficial ownership records. Each shareholding transfer or membership change in the LLC must be reflected in the Register of Members and registered with the National Business Registration Portal within 10 days of the transaction; the annual enterprise report filed by 31 March constitutes the de facto periodic confirmation of the current membership and controlling owners
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Legal Representatives
Minute Book of Members' Council Meetings and Resolutions
Register of Capital Contributions and Contribution Schedules

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300-800 per annum for registered office address, corporate secretarial services, and the registered agent agreement in a major commercial city such as Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,500-3,500 per annum for a statutory audit of financial statements of a mid-sized offshore software development LLC using a licensed Vietnamese independent audit firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Software production and high-tech enterprises may qualify for preferential CIT rates of 10% for 15 years or 15% for 10 years, plus CIT exemption for up to 4 years and 50% reduction for up to 9 subsequent years under Law No. 71/2014/QH13 and Decree No. 218/2013/ND-CP. Offshore development centers generally rely on standard 20% CIT unless located in qualifying high-tech zones or software parks with additional incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 02/TNDN (Final CIT Return) submitted via the General Department of Taxation's e-tax portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn) or the National Public Service Portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final CIT return and annual settlement must be filed no later than the 90th day from the end of the fiscal year; quarterly provisional CIT payments are due no later than the 30th day of the first month of the next quarter, with total provisional payments required to be at least 80% of the final annual liability

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification details including enterprise name, tax code, address, and fiscal year period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owned LLC must enter the Vietnamese tax identification number and full registered address in the license-issuing province; all identifiers must match the Enterprise Registration Certificate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from sales and services rendered
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue on an accrual basis in accordance with Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS); intercompany service revenue from offshore parent or affiliates must be documented under an executed cost-plus or TNMM transfer pricing policy
Expenses must have legitimate invoices and supporting contracts; intercompany charges require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation to be deductible
Computed as revenue less deductible expenses plus non-deductible adjustments; must reflect arm's length results for the Vietnamese resident entity
Losses may be offset against subsequent profits within 5 consecutive years; no carryback is permitted; transfer pricing adjustments may impact eligible loss amounts
Enter 20% for standard rate, or preferential rate codes if enterprise holds high-tech or software incentive certificates issued by the competent authority
Payable amount after applying tax credits and provisional quarterly payments; final settlement must reconcile cumulative quarterly payments with the annual return
Applicable where the Vietnamese entity derives foreign source income; credit is capped at the Vietnamese CIT payable on that foreign income and requires supporting tax certificates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary declaration adjustments for pricing, royalties, or interest paid to related parties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any adjustment arising from transfer pricing examinations or self-adjustment must reflect arm's length results and may attract late payment interest if underpaid

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from VND 2,000,000 to VND 10,000,000 depending on days of delay; late payment interest is 0.03% per day on the unpaid tax amount. Administrative fines for incorrect declarations causing underpayment can reach 20% of the underpaid amount plus 0.03% daily interest. Criminal sanctions apply only in cases of tax evasion under the Penal Code.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: There is no Vietnamese domestic withholding tax on dividends paid by a Vietnamese LLC to foreign shareholders. A resident shareholder repatriating profits must provide bank account documentation and evidence of audited financial statements. For jurisdictions where the Vietnam DTA imposes a residual withholding concept, the taxpayer must file Form 01/NTNN or a treaty relief application with the local tax authority before repatriation, submit the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, and obtain tax registration or approval for treaty benefit under Circular No. 80/2021/TT-BTC. The TRC must be legalized or apostilled, translated into Vietnamese, and submitted with the annual CIT finalization file for reduced treaty rates on interest, royalties, or service fees.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are subject to 10% deemed income WHT on the gross deemed profit under the foreign contractor tax regime, unless reduced under an applicable DTA. Interest paid to non-resident lenders attracts 5% CIT WHT on gross interest under the foreign contractor tax regime, with treaty rates typically capped at 10% for most DTA partners. Treaty relief requires TRC and application through the Vietnamese tax authority; loans must be registered and comply with thin capitalization rules (30% EBITDA interest limitation per Decree No. 132/2020/ND-CP).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File required when total related party transactions exceed VND 30 billion annually, or where the enterprise's total related party revenue exceeds VND 50 billion; a Country-by-Country Report applies to ultimate parent groups with consolidated revenue of at least VND 18,000 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam applies economic substance principles through transfer pricing rules under Decree No. 132/2020/ND-CP and Circular No. 45/2021/TT-BTC. Enterprises must demonstrate actual business substance, relevant personnel, and risk management capabilities supporting intercompany arrangements. The economic substance requirement applies specifically to offshore development centers: the Vietnamese entity must perform software development functions with adequate qualified employees, control over development activities, and assume economic risks commensurate with its reported income. Pure shell structures with minimal staff and no operational substance are subject to recharacterization of profits by the tax authority under taxpayer anti-avoidance provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Offshore development center undercharges software development services to foreign parent, accumulates persistent losses, or fails to maintain contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation demonstrating arm's length pricing; related-party loans exceed the 30% EBITDA interest-deduction ratio
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority may re-determine taxable income, apply deemed profits, disallow excess interest deductions, impose fines up to 20% of underpaid tax, and charge late payment interest at 0.03% per day. Penalties for failing to maintain documentation include fines from VND 25,000,000 to VND 50,000,000 plus potential profit adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and tax administration directors may be held personally liable for failure to file correct tax returns; criminal tax evasion penalties under the Penal Code range from VND 100,000,000 to VND 4,500,000,000 in fines and imprisonment of up to 7 years for deliberate underpayment exceeding thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing, receiving, or using illegal invoices to inflate deductible expenses, creating fictitious service contracts, or classifying ineligible costs as software development expenses; cash payments to fake sub-contractors without economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 20 times the illegal invoice value; tax underpayment penalties of 20% of evaded tax; business license suspension up to 3 months; criminal prosecution under Penal Code Article 200 with fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment from 6 months to 7 years depending on scale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false invoices or intentionally direct evasion face joint and several civil liability for unpaid tax, travel bans pending criminal proceedings, and imprisonment; courts may pierce the corporate veil when fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Vietnamese LLC used as conduit with minimal staff, no active software development operations, outsourced all core activity to third parties, and no decision-making or risk-bearing functions; profits routed without operational substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority may recharacterize transactions, reallocate profits to the ultimate parent, deny treaty benefits, impose anti-avoidance adjustments, and levy fines up to 20% of re-determined tax plus daily interest. Registration may be revoked under enterprise law for inactive companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal restitution orders for tax arrears where corporate assets are insufficient following fraudulent restructuring; entry bans and imprisonment may apply under anti-money laundering and tax evasion provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain proper corporate accounting records, incomplete entity register information, or cross-border transactions through unlicensed payment channels without underlying commercial documentation; large cash flows not matching software contract milestones
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the AML Law and banking regulations for non-reporting, unauthorized payment services, and violations of foreign exchange regulations; fines range from VND 100,000,000 to VND 3,000,000,000; corporate bank accounts may be frozen and licenses suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners failing AML obligations face personal fines and criminal charges for money laundering under Penal Code Articles 251-252, with imprisonment up to 15 years and personal seizure of assets.
